chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Ribāṭ, from Ibn Miskān, from Zurārah, who said:
I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say:

“The wall of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was a qāmah high, so when one cubit of its shadow had passed, he performed al-ẓuhr, and when two cubits of its shadow had passed, he performed al-ʿaṣr.”

Then he said: “Do you know why the one cubit and two cubits were set?” I said, “No.” He said: “For the sake of the obligatory prayer: when the time of one cubit and two cubits enters, you begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the supererogatory prayer.”

key_terms.ذِرَاعٌ: one cubit; a time marker based on shadow length
key_terms.ذِرَاعَانِ: two cubits; a later time marker based on shadow length
key_terms.فَيْئِهِ: its returning shadow used as a measure for prayer timing
key_terms.ٱلنَّافِلَةَ: the supererogatory prayer left aside once the obligatory prayer time enters
key_terms.ٱلْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory prayer that must be prioritized

ai.seo_question: Why were one cubit and two cubits set as markers for ẓuhr and ʿaṣr prayer times?
ai.summary: This hadith explains prayer timing in relation to shadow length at the mosque of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It clarifies that the markers of one cubit and two cubits were designated to prioritize the obligatory salat over the nafilah once those points in time are reached.
